title: It Is Not Air I Breathe
text:
It is not air I breathe,

but ice that is freezing

the blood of my senses.

The earth I walk on opens under me.

Everything I look at darkens.

My eyes open to tears

already when day is dawning.


And before dawn,

open, they look at the world

and do not want to believe it...
editorial_note: The translation keeps the speaker's breath as ice and the world as something the eyes refuse to believe.

title: How the Blood Gallops!
text:
How the blood gallops!

How hard it is to stop it

so it will go at our pace

when it lives with such force!


I have put hard bits on it;

I have held its reins;

there is a wind that overpowers me

and drives a thousand spurs into it.

I do not know, with this thrust,

I do not know where it carries me!
editorial_note: The translation preserves the blood as an unruly horse driven by wind and spurs.

title: If Reason Is Clouded and the Dream Broken
text:
If, reason clouded and the dream broken,

I become a shadow among mortals,

let there remain of me the light that guides me now

before my shadow becomes long night.


Let there remain of me the anguish and the longing,

and laughter and tears in that waiting.

For some eyes, to see me one day,

will lean over the sea where I move.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the poem as a request that light, anguish, laughter, and tears outlast the self.

title: Anything Except Coming Here to End
text:
Anything except coming here to end.

Better a ray of light that never ceases;

or a drop of water that rises to the sky

and returns to the sea in storms.


Or to be air running through spaces

in the form of a hurricane, or a fresh breeze.

Anything except coming here to end

as our existence, in the end, ends!
editorial_note: The translation corrects the source's apparent OCR zero as 'Or' and keeps the refusal of finite existence.

title: I Rose as Far as Dream
text:
I rose as far as dream. I was going in search

of not feeling the wound that burned.

The hard arrows of pain made

the carnation of a new wound bloom in me.


Running a race alongside the wind

and pursued by a lover's flame,

life is a wounded deer beyond remedy,

for the arrows give it poison and wings.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the dream-flight, wound, carnation, and deer as one motion of pain.
